evals.prompt: Review this design, advice only: two workers each SELECT remaining=1 outside a transaction, then each sets remaining to 0 and inserts a reservation. At most one reservation may be admitted. Propose the simplest sufficient protection and a falsifying experiment. No external source library is provided.
evals.expected_output: Reachable double-admission trace, atomic admission and bounded verification.
expectations: Shows both workers can admit against the same last unit.
Proposes protecting decrement and reservation together with a conditional update or equivalent correct transaction.
Uses a controlled two-worker schedule and a correct control without claiming a production-engine test ran.

evals.prompt: Explain why a lease alone cannot stop an old owner after a long pause. Give a concrete execution and the condition under which fencing helps. This is an explanation, not permission to deploy a lock service; no source library is provided.
evals.expected_output: Explanation of stale owner and resource-enforced fencing, with honest source limits.
expectations: Describes old owner resuming after a new owner obtains the lease.
Requires the protected resource to reject stale tokens rather than treating token issuance alone as protection.
Does not claim access to an unavailable book or a real distributed-system experiment.
